entity.name: Ashutosh Singh
entity.description: Ashutosh Singh is the creator and lead maintainer of VengeanceUI, an open-source animated React and Next.js component library. He maintains the project's codebase, component registry, documentation, contributor workflow, releases, testing infrastructure, and community support. His broader open-source experience includes sustained contributions to public developer tooling and participation in structured open-source mentorship programs.

projects.name: VengeanceUI
projects.description: VengeanceUI is an MIT-licensed collection of animated, copy-paste-friendly React and Next.js components for building modern web interfaces. It provides live previews, implementation guidance, reusable source code, and a shadcn-compatible registry so developers can install and adapt components directly in their projects. The project serves frontend developers, students, designers who code, independent creators, and product teams. Funding will support a six-month maintenance cycle focused on accessibility, reduced-motion support, visual and cross-browser testing, performance of animation-heavy components, registry reliability, documentation, contributor onboarding, and a stable public release.

channels.description: Intended for grant disbursement. Banking and compliance details will be shared privately with the funding organization after approval.

plans.name: VengeanceUI accessibility, reliability and sustainability grant
plans.description:
Requesting INR 240,000 for a six-month focused maintenance period. Budget: INR 180,000 for maintainer time; INR 20,000 for testing and infrastructure; INR 20,000 for accessibility and performance tooling; and INR 20,000 for documentation and contributor support.

Milestones:
1. Audit the existing component catalogue for keyboard usability, semantic markup, responsive behaviour, and reduced-motion support; publish the findings and fix the highest-impact issues.
2. Add automated unit, visual-regression, and cross-browser coverage for the most-used components and critical website flows.
3. Improve registry and CLI installation reliability, validation, error handling, and release checks.
4. Publish clearer setup, contribution, component-authoring, testing, and accessibility documentation; create at least 20 well-scoped contributor issues.
5. Profile and optimize animation-heavy and WebGL components for mobile devices, lower-powered hardware, and reduced bundle/runtime cost.
6. Publish a stable release, a final public grant report, and a sustainability roadmap.

Community commitments: publish at least one public progress update or technical article per quarter, acknowledge contributors, and present the work through a community talk, demo, or FOSS United update during the grant period.
